channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nscale Faces Pushback on $30 Billion IPO Valuation
item.description: Nscale, the data center developer backed by Nvidia, is facing opposition to the valuation target of about $30 billion that it’s pursuing in its IPO, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Ruhell Amin reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Musk Says He’ll Gift SpaceX Shares to ‘Every Kid in America’
item.description: Elon Musk pledged to distribute a share of SpaceX to each American child, posting the move just hours after artificial intelligence competitor Anthropic PBC said it would set aside a portion of its shares for the public benefit.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen

item.title: Don Wilson on the GPU Market's Trillion Dollar Question
item.description: When we spoke to Don Wilson, founder and CEO of DRW, in Chicago last year, he told us he wanted to build a market for GPUs that would eventually be bigger than oil. A year's time in the age of AI is an eternity, and so for the first episode of this year's Chicago live show - recorded at City Winery - Wilson joins us on stage again to talk about what's changed and what hasn't in his quest to help build this market. We get his take on the recent tech selloff, including credit concerns around neocloud CoreWeave. And we also discuss how DRW is developing a “crunch spread” (the GPU version of a crack spread), the latest on his plans to launch GPU futures, and the possibility of token futures too. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Indonesia Ends Radioactive Emergency After US Shrimp Scare
item.description: Indonesia declared an end to a yearlong emergency over radioactive contamination near Jakarta that affected exports of shrimp, cloves and sneakers, prompting US food recalls and unprecedented import restrictions.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara

item.title: Anti-AI Trade Drives Buyers Into Bonds: Market Analysis
item.description: Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie and Paul Dobson break down today's key themes for analysts and investors on "Bloomberg: The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Korea Data Center IPO to Test AI Investor Resolve After Tumult
item.description: Data-center infrastructure company Elice Inc. is poised to debut on South Korea’s tech-heavy Kosdaq market Tuesday, testing AI investors’ nerves after peer Firmus canceled its high-profile listing this month.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: JPMorgan Brings Deposit Token JPM Coin to Ethereum for Institutional Clients
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is launching its deposit token on Ethereum, extending the lender’s push into blockchain payments as Wall Street grows more comfortable moving money on public networks.
item.dc:creator: Anna Irrera

item.title: Norway Data Center Firm Hunts for Partner on Canada-Europe Fiber Link
item.description: Much of Canada’s data and voice traffic travels through US networks, but US threats against Canadian sovereignty have forced Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government to review this vulnerability.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dion

item.title: The Case for Buying Small Caps Now
item.description: After years of being overshadowed by US megacaps and the artificial intelligence boom, could smaller companies finally be ready for a comeback? Merryn Somerset Webb speaks with Downing fund manager Simon Evan-Cook and Odyssean Capital’s Stuart Widdowson about why small caps remain unusually cheap, what could bring investors back, and whether small-cap value could become the ultimate anti-AI trade. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix Slide Causes $137 Billion Hit to Korea Pension
item.description: South Korea’s main pension fund took a 182 trillion won ($137 billion) hit after a decline in stakes of equities including Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc.
item.dc:creator: Shinhye Kang

item.title: Cornell University’s Basu on US-China AI Race
item.description: Kaushik Basu, Professor at Cornell University and former Chief Economist at the World Bank, discusses the AI race between the US and China, and impact on the global economy. He speaks with Stephen Engle from the sidelines of the Bund Summit in Shanghai. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Selloff Nears Turning Point as Mag 7 Earnings Loom
item.description: The AI trade is in focus as Big Tech earnings are set to test investor sentiment on hyperscaler spending. Bloomberg's Sunny Bangia and Anthony Stephens as well as UBS Financial Adviser and Managing Director Xi Qiao discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Will Empower India's Space Missions, Says Minister
item.description: Jitendra Singh, the Indian science & technology minister says that artificial intelligence is a great advantage in empowering India's space missions. Speaking to Bloomberg's Shery Ahn, he says human-led intelligence will need to use AI optimally to charge nuclear and space programs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Says Claude AI Tool Triggered No Kings Instagram Suspension
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. said an automated security system mistakenly suspended the Instagram account of the No Kings Coalition at the height of a nationwide series of demonstrations.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Japan’s Nikkei Narrows Losses as Tech Woes Cool Ahead of Results
item.description: Japan’s tech-heavy Nikkei gauge narrowed its losses as investors began to look ahead to the earnings season in both Japan and the US.
item.dc:creator: Aya Wagatsuma and Momoka Yokoyama

item.title: Taiwan Dollar Bulls Look Past AI-Led Drop to Year-End Rally
item.description: The Taiwan dollar’s weakness led by global jitters over the artificial intelligence trade is masking the island’s underlying economic resilience that favors the currency’s rally into year-end, analysts say.
item.dc:creator: Jiefei Liu and Kaman Ng

item.title: Anthropic to Shift Some Shares Into New ‘Public Good’ Fund
item.description: Anthropic PBC said it plans to put 5% of its shares into a new so-called public benefit fund that allows it to make donations that can address “the public good,” including mitigating AI’s impact on the job market.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Manson

item.title: Inside Andreessen’s Growing Political Influence
item.description: Bloomberg Businessweek features writer Austin Carr tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Marc Andreessen became an increasingly influential Republican donor and adviser after years of shifting political allegiances, with disputes over AI, crypto and other Biden-era policies playing a role in his latest turn. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Carr explains how Andreessen has translated his Silicon Valley influence into Washington access while maintaining a political style that associates describe as more calculated than his combative online persona. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Woodside Pauses Scarborough Pre-Commissioning Due to Protest
item.description: Woodside Energy Group Ltd. said that pre-commissioning work at its $12 billion Scarborough liquefied natural gas export project off the coast of Western Australia was paused after Greenpeace protesters climbed aboard the gas platform.
item.dc:creator: Brett Miller and Keira Wright

item.title: AI Trade Reversal Pierces Asia’s Star Picks-and-Shovels Stocks
item.description: A deepening selloff in US technology stocks is exposing a new vulnerability in Asia’s artificial intelligence trade: mounting financing costs could choke off the spending needed to sustain the boom, threatening earnings across a supply chain that has powered the region’s stock-market rally.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Vishnoi, Charlotte Yang and Faseeh Mangi
